name: Leo I Dwarf
tagline: A Milky Way satellite 820,000 light-years out — so distant it was the first dwarf found purely on photographic survey plates.

facts.label: Notable
facts.value: Hosts a surprising central black hole

history: Leo I is one of the Milky Way's most remote classical satellites — so far out that astronomers long debated whether it was even bound to the galaxy. Gaia's proper motions confirmed it is, on a wide, plunging orbit. Its star-formation history is unusually prolonged for a spheroidal, with episodes into the last billion years. Leo I surprised everyone in 2021 when stellar motions suggested a central black hole of ~3 million solar masses — absurdly large for a dwarf its size.
